answer: Collateral bonding curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital in a smart contract vault before transacting. A consensus kernel inspects agent telemetry, slashing bonded deposits if clone behavior or equivocation is detected. Admitted identities are indexed on an onyx state ledger. An attacker incurs the verifiable capital cost of immobilizing substantial liquidity per identity. However, steep collateral requirements disadvantage capital-constrained, honest agents.
